findings.evidence: features/002-develop-skill/002-develop-skill-tasks.md — T5 ('Reviewer-driven lane re-check (catch-all) at Gate 4') and T5b ('Mechanical pre-Gate-4 lane recheck') are split across two tasks but both touch the same surface (the lane-recheck pipeline at the Phase B/C boundary in `skills/develop/SKILL.md`). The two acceptance criteria together verify AC-8 part (a) and AC-8 part (b); the dependency chain T3 → T5b → T10 → T5 means a single-author implementation will land them as adjacent diffs anyway. From the simplicity lens, this looks like over-decomposition: one shippable surface (the lane-recheck pipeline) split into two task entries.
findings.claim: Possible over-decomposition — two tasks track one shippable unit (the lane-recheck pipeline) (Simplicity First, 'Minimum surface that solves the problem'; applied at task-list level: minimum tasks that cover the requirements without creating bookkeeping overhead). T5 and T5b share a code surface (`skills/develop/SKILL.md` Phase B.1 / Phase C closer) and both verify halves of AC-8.
findings.proposed_change: Merge T5b into T5 as a sub-task with a numbered sub-acceptance (a) for the mechanical recheck and (b) for the reviewer-driven catch-all. Updated T5 acceptance: '(a) Before Gate 4 opens, the skill writes lane-recheck-{task-id}.json per the mechanical-recheck schema; (b) when a Gate 4 round-1 block finding references the lane assignment AND is accepted in Round 2, the manifest records re-lane forced and a fresh manifest opens.' Update the coverage matrix: R5 → T5, R5.1 → T5. Drop T5b.
